gen-fs-styro-gf-stack-sans-notch: Styro packs its lowercase tight, almost crowded, with a retro bark. It hits hardest where letters huddle together, while Stack Sans Notch is the sans that lets you see right into every curve.
gen-fs-styro-gf-tiktok-sans: Letters pressed so close they nearly touch give Styro its retro, commanding bite, set against TikTok Sans. Over a full page, the sans-serif's tall, spacious letters keep going down easily.
gen-fs-styro-gf-ubuntu-sans: Styro crowds its letters into a retro, commanding block, while Ubuntu Sans leaves its curves open, with tubular strokes. It earns its keep big and brief, a shout rather than talk.
gen-fs-styro-gf-yaldevi: Tight, retro and loud, with a commanding swagger: that's Styro. Its crowded letters meet Yaldevi's outsized lowercase and right-opening e, and that tight-against-open tension is the pair's real draw.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-julius-sans-one: Heavy and tightly packed, Tanker curls its open curves inward, while Julius Sans One spaces itself wide with open-ended curves. One slams the door, the other leaves it ajar.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-lexend-peta: Commanding and heavy, Tanker tucks its curves inward, while Lexend Peta opens wide with unthinned curves and a big x-height. Shrink Tanker and its weight clogs; enlarge Lexend Peta and it sprawls.
gen-fs-zina-fs-merriweather-sans: Fat downstrokes, hairline upstrokes, wide-set spacing: pure broad-nib drama. Zina is the show-off, Merriweather Sans the sans-serif beneath it, its tall lowercase making each word look sturdy and large.
gen-gf-abhaya-libre-fs-bespoke-sans: Traditional and dignified, all bold thicks and hairline thins. Abhaya Libre sets that weight against Bespoke Sans, a sharp sans with generous space between curve ends and stems and little stroke contrast.
gen-gf-bbh-hegarty-fs-literata: Pinched-neck bottles, fence-post spacing: that's BBH Hegarty. Literata, the text serif, steps in with sturdy thin lines, slightly heavier thick ones and wide, unclosed curves that undo the heading's closed-in look.
gen-gf-belanosima-fs-literata: Constant stroke, top to baseline: that's Belanosima. Literata, the text serif, brings sturdy thin lines, slightly heavier thick ones and wide, unclosed curves, and that fixed-versus-varying stroke contrast is the hook.
